messages:
sarah: Heads-up: Acme sees repeated 429s and tokenized latency on their dedicated pool redwood-ded-42 since ~03:00 UTC. They report successful calls turning into 429s even at low sustained QPS. Tagging @eli @mike for visibility.
eli: On it — do we have tenant id and sample request IDs? Any customer repro steps or curl snippets?
sarah: Tenant is tenant-acme-123. Sample request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Customer ran a quick curl loop and hits 429 after ~120 requests. They also say console shows 10 r/s but our backend math shows 600/min, so I suspect a unit/denom mismatch on quota conversion.
mike: I pulled the quota row from kv-store: rate_units=600, denom=minute. Serving code expects denom=second in some code paths — looks like a migration path left denom as minute without conversion. If true, effective enforcement ends up 600 r/s vs intended 10 r/s or vice-versa depending on path. I'll investigate mapping logic.
nora: Customer repro (they sent this): ```sh
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"; \
done
```
eli: Reproduced on staging using tenant-acme-123 config. Server logs show throttle decision from quota_evaluator.go:142 -> response 429 reason="rate_limit_exceeded". The quota row on staging has denom=minute and burst_window=30s, which makes bursts look larger/smaller depending on which denom path is used.
mike: Root cause summary: plan-migrate job inserted denom=minute for legacy plans but the dedicated rate limiter expects denom=second; conversion code path missing for dedicated pools. Quick mitigation: apply transient mapping that treats denom=minute as units/60 for dedicated pools, and increase burst_window to 60s to smooth parallel clients. I'll prepare a config patch.
sarah: Before the patch, can we ask the customer to hold off producing new load? Also log the exact request ids they provided.
autoscale-bot: deploy started: config/autoscale/patch#4770 by mike. Rolling to redwood-ded-42 (3/3 nodes) — ETA ~2m.
mike: Patch applied to redwood-ded-42. Monitoring: error rate dropped from ~8% -> 0.5%, p95 latency from 2.4s -> 0.9s. There are still rare spikes when the customer runs 50 parallel clients, looks like noisy neighbor smoothing needed.
nora: Customer confirmed fewer 429s in the last 10m. They still observe occasional spikes under high concurrency; asked if we can do per-tenant smoothing or soft-rate throttles.
eli: Follow-ups created: 1) migration script to normalize denom for all affected plans 2) unit-tests for denom->rate mapping 3) add integration test for dedicated burst behavior 4) ops runbook step to communicate rollback. I'll file the JIRA and assign.
sarah: Thanks all. I'll update the CS ticket and tell Acme we've rolled a mitigation and will run a full migration. If we find measurable customer impact we'll offer SLA credit. Closing this Slack thread after ticket update.
